use_case_name: Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU shall extrapolate the received target's position to the time of transmission when reporting on the Surveillance NPG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific objective for the C² JU in handling target data, which contributes to the high-level goal of defining reference points and geometric areas by ensuring positional accuracy over time.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU has the responsibility to determine whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU must have received a J12.6 Target Sorting message from a non-C² JU for a track that was not locally acquired before it can assign an initial TQ value and extrapolate the target's position to the time of transmission.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific system state (receipt of external data via a specific message type) that must hold before the C² JU can perform actions related to defining reference points or geometric areas based on that track data.

evidence_cards.content: The unit originating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report always retains reporting responsibility.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the system state regarding reporting authority that must hold before defining reference points/areas (AOP/Fix).

evidence_cards.content: Emergency alerts are not used on reference points, lines, or areas.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a system state constraint that must hold before defining reference points and geometric areas — it precludes the use of emergency alerts in this context, forming a precondition for valid area/point definition operations.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to the restricted TQ value 'e' shall not be automatically correlated.

evidence_cards.content: To prevent confusion and possible misunderstanding, any change to data concerning any point comprising a portion of a segmented line or multisided area shall cause the entire line or area to be transmitted by the reporting JU. Receiving units shall purge the previously held segmented line or multisided area and replace it with the new report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines mandatory system behavior during modification of geometric areas in the main flow: full retransmission and replacement upon any point change.

evidence_cards.content: The TNs used to initiate the segmented line or multisided area shall be transmitted for every report of the segmented line or multisided area, including a change of R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that Track Numbers must accompany every update report in the main flow, ensuring continuity of reference across modifications.

evidence_cards.content: The Reference TN of the first J3.0 message with Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to value 0 shall be used as the only legal identifier for all subsequent references to the segmented line or multisided area, except when dropping the line or area, setting/clearing the Force Tell Indicator, or responding to a Data Update Request by TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the canonical identifier rule for ongoing interaction sequences involving segmented lines or multisided areas — critical for maintaining consistent referencing throughout the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field in the initial word shall be set to value 2, Line, when describing a segmented line and shall be set to value 3, Multi-point Area, when describing a multisided area.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines required field values for initiating geometric area definitions in the main flow, constraining how the actor specifies the type of geometry being created.

evidence_cards.content: When defining an area that is a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse a J3.0I/J3.0E0/J3.0C2, J3.5I/J3.5E0/J3.5C3, or a J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence is used. The Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field in the J3.0I word shall be set to value 1, Single Point Area. The Square/Circle Switch field indicates that either a square or rectangle is being described when set to value 1 or indicates either a circle or ellipse is being described when set to value 2. A square or circle is being described, depending on the value of the Square/Circle Switch, when the Area Major Axis and Area Minor Axis fields are equal. When the axes are not equal, a rectangle or ellipse is described, depending on the value of the Square/Circle Switch. The orientation of the major axis with respect to True North is provided by the Axis Orientation Field.

evidence_cards.content: For slaved points or areas, the range between the slaved point/area center and Related TN remains constant; if J3.0C4 word is not included, bearing is a constant true bearing from J3.0C2 Related TN; if J3.0C4 word is included, bearing is relative to the course of J3.0C4 Related 1 TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines core interaction logic for defining slaved reference points/areas — specifies how system interprets presence/absence of J3.0C4 word to determine bearing type (true vs. relative) while maintaining constant range, which is part of the main flow for defining slaved geometry.

evidence_cards.content: Moving points, lines, and areas are reported by setting Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word to other than No Statement; the host extrapolates them to time of transfer to terminal; Time (Hour and Minute) and Time Function may also be reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the standard procedure (main flow step) for reporting non-slaved moving geometry — actor sets specific fields (Course/Speed ≠ No Statement), system performs extrapolation, optional time reporting — this is the canonical success path for defining moving reference elements.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the identifier assignment step for segmented lines/areas.

evidence_cards.content: The Square/Circle Switch field indicates that either a square or rectangle is being described when set to value 1, or indicates either a circle or ellipse is being described when set to value 2.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the step for configuring the bearing type for slaved points.

evidence_cards.content: Moving points, lines, and areas are reported by setting Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word to other than No Statement.

evidence_cards.content: Periodic updates following the original or retransmitted message shall be transmitted with the Periodic Report Indicator set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the subsequent step in the main flow for maintaining reference point information via periodic updates.

evidence_cards.content: To report an Area of Probability (AOP), the C2 JU uses a J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence as a minimum, with the J3.7I word transmitted with the FIX BRG field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific message sequence and field constraints required for the system to process the definition of a geometric area.

evidence_cards.content: When an AOP results from previously reported LOBs or from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, it shall be assigned a new TN, not one of the TNs assigned to the source data.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the exception handling in the main flow where an existing track is modified into a geometric area, preserving continuity.

evidence_cards.content: In response to a Data Update Request (J7.1 with ACT=0), the C² JU which originated the data or has R² for a J3.0 multi-point area/multi-segmented line shall respond with J3.0, J3.7 and/or J6.0 Amplification messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific message exchange sequence (Response step) in the main flow where the system responds to a request for reference point data.

evidence_cards.content: When responding with J3.0, J3.7 and/or J6.0 Amplification messages, the Response Indicator field shall be set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a mandatory parameter setting (Response Indicator = 1) required during the execution of the normal interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If the Reference Point Filter Indicator is set, the only other Filter Indicators that may be set are the SPI and Simulation Filter Indicators and, if required, a Geographic Area Filter.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the valid filter combinations when defining reference points, which constrains the interaction sequence for setting up reference point filters.

evidence_cards.content: EW product information filters shall be requested/reported in separate J7.6 messages from tracks and points except that if the Unknown E/C filter is set, then Unknown EW product information are filtered regardless of the setting of the EW Filter Indicator.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies how EW product information filters interact with geographic area definitions, affecting the main flow when EW data is involved.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the EW Filter Indicator is set, then all EW Fixes within/out the area and all EW AOPs having their center within/out the area and all EW LOBs with origin within/out the area are filtered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the filtering behavior when combining geographic area filters with EW indicators, which affects how geometric areas are applied to EW data during definition.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the Reference Point Filter Indicator is set, then all points within/out the area, all lines with all points within/out the area, and all areas completely within/out the area are filtered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the comprehensive filtering effect when both geographic area and reference point filters are active, defining the scope of what gets included/excluded in the defined geometry.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.5 message provides the capability to describe a circle/ellipse about a ground point, which would normally be used in reporting a SAM site but could be used with any J3.5 point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative geometric reporting format (circle/ellipse) available within the standard J3.5 reporting flow for fixed ground units.

evidence_cards.content: In addition to reporting points, the J3.0 message has the capability to transmit lines such as FEBAs and roads, areas such as search and exercise areas, and volumes such as corridors.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes alternative geometric shapes (lines, areas, volumes) that can be defined and transmitted via the J3.0 message, diverging from simple point reporting.

evidence_cards.content: If a segmented line is formed by joining 2 or 3 points, a single J3.0 message is used where the Line/Area Continuation Indicator is set to No Statement, the End Point field is set to value 1, and the Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field is set to value 2 (Line).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific alternative flow for creating simple segmented lines using a single message.

evidence_cards.content: If a segmented line or multisided area is formed by joining more than 3 points, multiple J3.0 messages are used, each with a unique Track Number (TN), where the second and all subsequent messages have the Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the alternative flow for complex geometries requiring message chaining.

evidence_cards.content: In the flow for more than 3 points, the point location in the extension word of the second and subsequent messages must match the last point location of the previous message to assure receipt of all transmissions.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a validation constraint within the multi-message alternative flow.

evidence_cards.content: When describing a multisided area with more than 3 points, the last point location transmitted must be the same as the initial point location to close the figure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the closure condition for the multisided area alternative flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for a reference point, line, or area, the R² unit is declared inactive.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This represents an alternative flow where the reporting responsibility is terminated prematurely due to a specific system message, diverging from the standard periodic update cycle.

evidence_cards.content: If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² for the point, line, or area using the same Reference TN(s).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow for handling missed updates, allowing a transfer of reporting responsibility after a specific timeout threshold.

evidence_cards.content: When a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix shall be used for the new AOP.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative flow path that diverges from the main flow step of assigning a new TN; instead of generating a new TN, the system reuses the existing one when converting a fix to an AOP.

evidence_cards.content: If a change of Environment/Category is proposed by a J7.0 (ACT=1) message and accepted by the R² JU operator, the original Track Number (TN) is retained, and the entity is reported in the appropriate J3.x surveillance message.

source_locations.location: LEGEND section, definition of 'S = SAME TN'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative flow where the system diverges from assigning a new track number to retaining the existing one upon acceptance of a category change proposal.

evidence_cards.content: If a proposed Environment/Category change is accepted by the R² JU, the system shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT=0) drop track message for the original Track Number and report the entity as a new Track Number in the appropriate J3.x surveillance message or J5.4 message.

source_locations.location: LEGEND section, definition of 'N = NEW TN'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative flow where the system diverges from simple updates to a mandatory re-identification process involving dropping the old track and creating a new one.

evidence_cards.content: If an Area of Probability (AOP) is formed from a single fix, the same Track Number shall be retained; if an AOP is formed from 2 or more fixes, a new Track Number shall be assigned.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a conditional alternative flow for defining geometric areas (AOP) based on the number of source fixes, determining whether to retain the current track or start a new one.

evidence_cards.content: For Data Report Type 4 (Datum), the same Track Number may be used by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies an optional alternative path allowing track number continuity for specific data types via manual operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the EW Filter Indicator is set, then all EW Fixes within/out the area and all EW AOPs having their center within/out the area and all EW LOBs with origin within/out the area are filtered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative filtering behavior for EW product information when combined with geographic area filters — a valid variant path that diverges from standard reference point or track-based filtering flows.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the Reference Point Filter Indicator is set, then all points within/out the area, all lines with all points within/out the area, and all areas completely within/out the area are filtered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow for filtering reference points/lines/areas based on geographic containment — a distinct operational path from non-geographic or single-indicator filtering scenarios.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found for a received J2 PPLI report, the C² JU shall integrate the report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture; if no subsequent J2 messages are received and the C² JU still has no local data, it assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception flow where the system fails to correlate data and subsequently disclaims responsibility, which is a specific error handling path.

evidence_cards.content: If position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated; after decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, and report the PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator and PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator fields as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow triggered by data inconsistency (decorrelation), specifying the recovery action of creating a new track with specific field values set to 'No Statement'.

evidence_cards.content: To prevent confusion and possible misunderstanding, any change to data concerning any point comprising a portion of a segmented line or multisided area shall cause the entire line or area to be transmitted by the reporting JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory system response to data modification during geometric definition, acting as an exception handler for partial updates.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving units shall purge the previously held segmented line or multisided area and replace it with the new report when a change occurs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific recovery behavior required of receiving units to handle the exception of mid-stream data changes.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point, line, or area shall not be required to purge the point, line, or area; however, if it does not purge, it shall assume R² for that entity to ensure it remains active on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception handling behavior when a termination message is received but not acted upon — a deviation from expected purging flow that requires compensatory assumption of responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU fails to receive the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for emergency points and further updates are not received, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies timeout-based exception recovery path for emergency point termination when expected termination message is missing — an error condition handled via time-bound fallback purging.

evidence_cards.content: Values accepted for retransmission shall be retransmitted if the JU assumes R², unless the JU holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) for the field which differs from the value accepted for retransmission.

source_locations.location: Paragraph under section 4.4.4.7 IDENTITY DATA, starting 'Values accepted for retransmission...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition to the standard retransmission flow where the C2 JU must deviate from retransmitting accepted values based on the presence of conflicting locally derived data.

evidence_cards.content: In the latter case [where JU holds differing non-NS locally derived data], the JU shall report the locally derived data.

source_locations.location: Paragraph under section 4.4.4.7 IDENTITY DATA, sentence following the exception trigger.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory system response/action when the exception condition is met: reporting local data instead of retransmitting.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.7.2 ELECTRONIC WARFARE PRODUCT INFORMATION REPORTING RESPONSIBILITY, paragraph 1

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a hard constraint/exception condition where the system must prevent a user from taking over responsibility for a track generated by another unit, enforcing data integrity and accountability.

evidence_cards.content: When another JU assumes R² (responsibility) for a point, line, or area that has an active force tell alert, it shall transmit the appropriate FT IND value as previously received in the J3.0 message to maintain the alert state.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the system's response to an unexpected condition (change of responsibility) during the definition/maintenance of reference points/areas, ensuring continuity of alerts rather than failure.

evidence_cards.content: Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.0 message with FT IND set to value 0, providing an alternative recovery path to the standard J7.0 termination message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies an optional exception flow for clearing alerts that deviates from the primary termination sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If an R² shift occurs during execution of a Data Update Request (DUR) response where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R² shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (R² shift during DUR) that prevents the responding unit from completing the update sequence for prior requests.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful completion, each point, line, or area reported on the interface shall be assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory state of the system regarding track number assignment for the defined entity.

evidence_cards.content: The position of the defined reference point or geometric area shall be reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the required data format and content stored in the system for the entity's location.

evidence_cards.content: If altitude/elevation is required, it is reported; time associated with the point, line, or area is reported in hours/minutes, with meaning defined by the Time Function field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes additional state attributes (altitude, time) that must exist in the system if applicable to the definition.

evidence_cards.content: For segmented lines or multisided areas formed by more than 3 points, multiple messages are used, and the last point location transmitted must be the same as the initial point location to close the figure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific topological state required for closed multisided areas after successful reporting.

evidence_cards.content: The originator of a J3.0 or J3.5 (PTI = 0) point, line, or area retains reporting responsibility (R²) as long as the originator remains active and reports the entity.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the postcondition state for reporting responsibility retention after defining reference points/areas.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a condition that changes the postcondition state by terminating reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² for the point, line, or area using the same Reference TN(s).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the timeout-based transfer of reporting responsibility as a possible post-use-case state change.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a point, line, or area for which it had reporting responsibility, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory action to terminate reporting responsibility, leading to the postcondition of inactivity.

evidence_cards.content: The range of TQs used in determining correlation windows may be restricted by Min TQ and Max TQ values.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a potential system state constraint or configuration setting regarding Track Quality limitations that applies after the definition of reference points/areas (specifically for correlation logic).

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of the use case, the C2 JU has reported a Target Position Quality (TPQ) value that corresponds to the calculated probability area (S) according to Table 4.4-7 or the S-to-TPQ relationship table, and if Variable Track Quality (VTQ) is activated, any calculated TQ exceeding the manually entered maximum value is reported as that entered value.

source_locations.location: Page 49: Table 4.4-7; Page 50: S-to-TPQ table and section 4.4.4.12 Variable Track Quality
Page 49: Table 4.4-7; Page 50: S-to-TPQ table and section 4.4.4.12 Variable Track Quality

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state after successful reporting — specifically, the TPQ/TQ values assigned based on probability area calculations and VTQ constraints — which constitutes the postcondition of defining and reporting an AOP or geometric area.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful definition of an EW fix from previously reported LOBs, a new Track Number (TN) is assigned to the fix, which is then used for all subsequent updates.

source_locations.location: Page 84, paragraph starting 'An EW fix results from...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting system state (new TN assignment and update logic) after successfully defining an EW fix.

evidence_cards.content: When an Area of Probability (AOP) is changed to a fix, the TN of the previously reported AOP is retained and used for the new fix.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific postcondition regarding TN retention when transitioning from an AOP to a fix.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful reporting of an AOP resulting from previously reported LOBs, a new TN is assigned to the AOP, not one of the TNs assigned to the LOBs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the postcondition that the AOP possesses a unique TN distinct from its source LOBs.

evidence_cards.content: The new TN assigned to the AOP shall be used for all subsequent updates of the AOP.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the persistence of the new TN as the identifier for future updates.

evidence_cards.content: If an AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, a new TN is assigned to the AOP.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the postcondition for TN assignment when merging multiple fixes into an AOP.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful completion of defining a reference point or geometric area (including AOP), all receiving JUs shall accept the alert in their databases if an emergency or force tell alert was initiated via J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages with EMG IND or FT IND set appropriately.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state after successful alert initiation on tracks — specifically that receiving units have accepted and stored the alert in their databases, which is part of post-use-case system state for track-based alerts associated with defined areas/points.

evidence_cards.content: After termination of an emergency or force tell alert on a track (via J7.0 ACT=3 or 4 message), all receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of that message; optionally, alerts may also be cleared by reception of a J3.X message with EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the terminal system state after alert clearance — receiving units’ databases reflect removal of the alert condition, which constitutes a valid postcondition when the use case includes alert lifecycle management as part of defining reference geometry with associated alerts.

evidence_cards.content: After the C2 JU assumes R² of an IU (which occurs when reporting rules for a real-time track are met), it reports the entity as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the immediate system state and visibility of the entity after the use case completes successfully.

evidence_cards.content: The Identity shall be reported as Friend, and the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact data values assigned to the entity in the post-use-case state.

evidence_cards.content: After successfully defining a slaved point or area, the system state is such that the position is established as Delta Latitude and 1/Delta Longitude from the Related TN at the time of the report, with the Slaved Indicator set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific observable system state (position calculation method and indicator setting) immediately following the successful definition of a slaved entity.

evidence_cards.content: For non-slaved moving points, lines, and areas, the system state after definition involves extrapolation by the host to the time of transfer to the terminal, based on reported Course and Speed values.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the resulting system state for moving entities, specifically the requirement for host-side extrapolation to ensure accurate positioning at the time of data transfer.

evidence_cards.content: The originator of a J3.0 or J3.5 (PTI = 0) point, line, or area retains reporting responsibility (R²) as long as the originator remains active and reports the entity.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-use-case system state regarding persistent reporting responsibility after successful definition of reference points/lines/areas.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive; alternatively, if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² by operator action only using the same Reference TN(s).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies conditions under which the post-use-case state changes — either termination of responsibility or transfer to another unit — affecting data persistence and visibility.

evidence_cards.content: The latest IU to report on a reference or land (ground) point, line, or area has R² for that entity.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms final system state: reporting responsibility resides with the most recent reporting unit, ensuring data ownership and visibility are assigned post-successful completion.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of defining a reference point, line, or area (including AOP), the entity remains active on the interface unless explicitly purged; if a JU receives a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message but does not purge the entity, it shall assume R² for that entity to ensure it remains active.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-use-case system state: defined geometric entities persist as active on the interface unless terminated by explicit ACT=0 and subsequent purge; failure to purge implies assumption of reporting responsibility to maintain activity.

evidence_cards.content: Emergency points are normally terminated via the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when the emergency ceases; if no such message is received and no further updates occur, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies termination/purge behavior for emergency-related geometry — though excluded from scope per goal constraint, this confirms general lifecycle rules for reference entities and reinforces that non-emergency reference points/areas remain active until explicitly deactivated or timed out.

evidence_cards.content: Time associated with a reported point, line, or area (e.g., establishment, activation, deactivation) applies to the entire line or area if defined by multiple Reference TNs; if transmitted with subsequent segments/sides, it must match the first segment’s time and Time Function.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that temporal metadata attached during definition becomes part of the persistent state of the geometric entity and governs its interpretation across all segments — supporting the notion that the defined entity carries contextual state (time + function) post-completion.

evidence_cards.content: The system state after successfully defining a reference point or geometric area is that the C2 JU has reported the entity (e.g., AOP, line, area) with all required parameters (such as TN, position, time) and ensured that no emergency alert is associated with it.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.5.1, paragraph following 'TRACK REPORTING CRITERIA' heading

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the observable outcome of successful track reporting for subsurface surveillance entities, which includes reference points/geometric areas like AOPs — directly satisfying the postcondition requirement for system state after use case completion.

evidence_cards.content: All data reported for subsurface surveillance tracks (including reference points/areas) shall be time tagged, ensuring temporal consistency and traceability in the system state post-reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Time tagging is a mandatory attribute of reported track data; its presence confirms the system has achieved a consistent, auditable state after successful reporting — a key postcondition for operational validity.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful completion of defining an AOP (whether from organic data, LOBs, or EW fix analysis), the system state includes a new Track Number (TN) assigned to the AOP, which is used for all subsequent updates.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the persistent system state (assignment of a TN) resulting from the use case.

evidence_cards.content: If an AOP results from previously reported LOBs or fixes of differing TNs, the postcondition is that a new TN is assigned and used for all subsequent updates, distinct from the original TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the specific system state change (new TN assignment) required when merging multiple sources into a single geometric area.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message on a specific TN, the JU(s) that have originated surveillance amplification data on the track shall respond with the J6.0 Amplification message containing all available data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-use-case system state where surveillance amplification data is transmitted to requesting units upon successful completion of the reference point/area definition and subsequent update request.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU with R² for the Reference TN shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message upon receipt of a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that after defining reference points or areas, the system responds to ballistic missile update requests by transmitting appropriate space track data, indicating successful integration into the tracking system.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU responds with a J3.0, J3.7 and/or a J6.0 Amplification message, the Response Indicator field in these messages shall be set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the system sets the Response Indicator field to value 1 in response messages, confirming that the defined reference points or geometric areas are being reported as part of a successful use case execution.
